name: Groove Lab
threading: Pure functions; thread-safe; grooveShift is noexcept and allocation-free. apply() sorts and belongs on the message thread.
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/groove -B build/groove && cmake --build build/groove && ctest --test-dir build/groove
summary: Playback-time groove: MPC-style swing (50 to 75 percent of a step pair on a 16th or 8th grid), per-role push/pull, seeded humanize of time and velocity, a 16-cell accent curve and eight named templates. A groove never edits stored events; the caller applies grooveShift (or apply) once when it builds a playback snapshot or a MIDI file.
public_api: `Groove` (enabled, template, swing, grid, push/pull per role class, humanize time and velocity, seed, accent, bake flag) and `makeTemplate`
`grooveShift(groove, role, tick, eventIndex, ticksPerBar, stepsPerBar, loopIndex)` -> `Shift{ticks, velScale}`
`apply(groove, FlatEventList&, loopTicks, ticksPerBar, stepsPerBar, roleOf)` shifts a flattened pattern
`serialize` / `parse`: the 46-byte project-state form; `sanitized` clamps every field
limits: Shifts are limited to less than half a groove step so events never swap order
Swing is defined per step pair of the pattern's own step grid (16th or 8th variant)
adapters: Pass a function from chop to RoleClass (use classOf(DrumRole))
adapter_notes: The groove is playback-time only: call apply() on the flattened list before you build your playback, and pass the same Groove to your MIDI writer.
removal: Delete the folder and the composition hook (composition/src/groove.cpp); patterns are unaffected because a groove never writes into them.
